packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — Office365 `createEvent` was not updated to the new `createEvent(event, credentialId)` contract and always uses the first array entry, so for a second host's Office365 credential it posts to `/me/calendars/<first host's externalId>/events` with the second host's token, which returns 404 and that host gets no event (P1, conf 75; verbatim: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`)

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156 — The CalDAV/Apple base service ignores `credentialId` and filters each host's own calendar list by the first host's `externalId`, so for every other host the filter matches nothing, `Promise.all([])` succeeds, and it returns a success uid; a booking reference is saved for an event that was never created (P1, conf 75; verbatim: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`)

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — Lark `createEvent` still takes only `(event)` and always writes to the first host's `calendarId`, so another host's Lark credential calls the API against a calendar it does not own and event creation fails for that host (P1, conf 75; verbatim: `const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`)

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 — `credentialId` was added as a required parameter, but TypeScript still accepts implementations that declare fewer parameters, so Office365, Lark and BaseCalendarService compile without ever reading it; the compiler cannot catch them routing every host to the first destination (P2, conf 75; verbatim: `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>;`)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:370 — Which calendar gets written and which calendar gets recorded come from two different places: the `externalId` saved on the reference is `destination.externalId`, but the calendar service picks the target itself (Google by the first `credentialId` match, the others by array entry 0), so references can store a calendar the event was never created in and later updates/deletes go to the wrong calendar (P2, conf 75; verbatim: `const createdEvent = await createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId);`)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Video references lost their credential link: the old code saved `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results, the new code saves `undefined`, so handleCancelBooking.ts:491 (`if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`) skips `deleteMeeting` and new Zoom/Daily meetings are never deleted when a booking is cancelled (P1, conf 75; verbatim: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined,`)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208 — `updateLocation` builds replacement references from `updateEvent` results, which never set `externalId` or `credentialId`, so after a location edit the new calendar references have no calendar id and no credential id and later cancels/reschedules fall back to the legacy loop over all credentials and the "primary" calendar (P1, conf 75; verbatim: `externalCalendarId: result.externalId,`)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — The fallback is dead code: it only runs when `externalCalendarId` is empty and then searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals that empty value, so it always returns undefined; updates for references with no stored calendar id (legacy rows and rows rewritten by `updateLocation`) now send `calendarId: undefined` instead of the destination calendar and fail (P1, conf 75; verbatim: `: event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`)

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new fallback for `updateEvent` (and similarly for `deleteEvent`) is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
```

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:353 — createAllCalendarEvents now loads any destinationCalendar credential straight from the DB by id with no check that it belongs to the organizer or a host of this booking, and it ignores the `invalid` flag, so a stale or non-host credential gets used to write the event (attendee names/emails, notes) into that user's calendar. Before, those credentials were silently skipped. Example: an eventType.destinationCalendar set by a team admin or by a member who has since left the team, on a round-robin or collective event (P2, conf 50; verbatim: `const credentialFromDB = await prisma.credential.findUnique({ ... where: { id: destination.credentialId } })`)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, the new logic iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and, when it can’t find the matching credential in `this.calendarCredentials`, it now fetches it directly from the DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` and then proceeds to call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. The diff shows no validation that the fetched credential belongs to the organizer/any host for this booking (e.g., matching `userId`/`teamId` against the booking context), and no check to skip credentials marked `invalid` (it copies `invalid` into the constructed object but still uses it). Previously, if the credential wasn’t present in `this.calendarCredentials`, it would not create an event for that destination at all (i.e., effectively skipped). This is a real behavior change that can cause events/attendee data/notes to be written using a credential that isn’t part of the active host credentials set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:423 — No test covers cancelling a multi-host booking: for recurring bookings the loop re-runs, once per reference, the delete across all of the organizer's calendar credentials and each booking's first `_calendar` reference, so deletes repeat and other hosts' events are never deleted, and no assertion checks this (P2, conf 75; verbatim: `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) {`)

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the refactor changes `bookingCalendarReference` from a single `find(...)` to `filter(...)` and then loops: `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) { ... }`. Inside the recurring-booking branch it ignores the current `reference` and instead iterates over *all* `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and, for each updated booking, deletes only the *first* `_calendar` reference via `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. With multiple `_calendar` references (multi-host / multi-calendar), this can (a) re-run the same deletion work once per outer `reference`, causing duplicate deletes, and (b) never delete non-first calendar references for each booking, so some hosts’ calendar events may be left undeleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — This fallback can never find anything (it only runs when `externalCalendarId` is empty, then looks for a calendar whose externalId equals that empty value), so updates and deletes (also line 317) now go to `undefined` instead of the old destination calendar's externalId, and no test covers updating or deleting without an externalCalendarId (P2, conf 75; verbatim: `: event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`)

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute a fallback calendar id like:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

This `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to `externalCalendarId` in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy/empty, so it will almost always return `undefined` and fail to fall back to any destination calendar from `event.destinationCalendar`. In the pre-change code, the fallback used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly (single object), so this is a regression in behavior for calls where `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided/usable.
